old_caption:
The video showcases a close-up view of a watermelon slice, cut in half to reveal its juicy interior. The watermelon is positioned against a plain white background, emphasizing its vibrant red flesh and green rind. Throughout the sequence, the temperature and humidity levels are displayed in the top right corner, indicating a gradual decrease in temperature from 32°C/89°F to 31°C/87°F over the course of the video. The relative humidity (RH) fluctuates slightly between 47% and 55%. 

Initially, the watermelon appears fresh and ripe, with a bright red color and a few scattered seeds visible in the center. As time progresses, subtle changes in the watermelon's appearance become noticeable. The red hue of the flesh remains consistent, and the texture of the rind does not visibly change in firmness or wrinkling. By the end of the video, the watermelon maintains its overall shape and appearance.

caption:
The video showcases a single crescent-shaped watermelon wedge resting on a plain, evenly lit off-white surface. Its cut face shows red flesh with embedded pale seeds, a glossy wet area on the left, a pale yellow inner rind, and a thin green outer rim. The wedge remains roughly centered, with no obvious translation or rotation. Very subtle drying changes accumulate on its exposed surfaces, and the plain background stays largely unchanged throughout the visible segment.

The red flesh keeps a broadly similar appearance, with only slight changes in sheen and color as the visible drying continues. The lower rind stays pale yellow, and a small bead of juice appears near the lower-right edge, remaining visible and shifting slightly through the later portion without the slice itself moving. No event interrupts the scene; the wedge stays fixed while the surface slowly changes.

draft_caption:
The video showcases a single crescent-shaped watermelon wedge resting on a plain, evenly lit off-white surface. Its cut face shows red flesh with embedded pale seeds, a glossy wet patch on the left, a pale yellow inner rind, and a thin green outer rim. The wedge remains centered and stationary, with no visible translation or rotation. Subtle drying changes clearly accumulate on its exposed surfaces, and the plain background itself stays unchanged throughout the visible segment.

The red flesh gradually loses its wet sheen, becoming more matte and grainy, most noticeably on the left side, while its color appears slightly duller as the visible drying continues. The lower rind develops more yellowish, mottled patches, and a small dark bead of juice appears near the lower-right edge, remaining visible through the later portion without the slice moving. No event interrupts the scene; the wedge stays fixed while the drying surface changes.
